name: Hallmark
tagline: A design skill that teaches your AI coding tool to build web pages that don't look AI-generated.
sentence: Install one file, type /hallmark, and your coding assistant builds a web page using 50 real design themes with proper typography, spacing, and photography - then reviews the result in a browser to catch common AI-design patterns.

visual.alt: A design portfolio site for Field Office, a Copenhagen brand studio, showing precise wordmark typography with Hedvig Letters Serif measured at x-height 520, cap height 700, ascender 800, and baseline 0. The layout uses elegant serif type, muted earth tones, and careful letter spacing.
visual.caption: One of Hallmark's 50 themes - precise typography and real design decisions, not AI defaults.

board.say: When AI builds a web page, the result often looks generic - the same fonts, the same layout, the same stock-photo feel that screams 'a machine made this'.
You type /hallmark followed by what you want to build, or /hallmark redesign to fix an existing page.
A description of the page you want, or a path to an existing page you want redesigned.
The skill guides your AI through a design process, then reviews the result in a browser.
steps: Picks a theme from 50 material-based design systems (or creates a custom one from your prompt)
Builds the page with proper typography, color, spacing, and about 755 openly licensed photos from Wikimedia Commons
Opens the finished page in a browser and runs a lint pass to catch common AI design patterns
Flags anything that looks machine-made (generic gradients, centered everything, stock-photo layouts) and fixes it

board.say: A web page that looks like a designer made it.

outputs.eg: A hotel website with serif typography, hand-illustrated artwork, and a color palette based on earth tones
The lint pass caught 3 AI-slop patterns (centered hero, generic gradient, no real photography) and fixed them

before: AI builds a web page and it looks like every other AI-generated page - centered text, blue gradients, generic stock photos
You ask the AI to 'make it look better' and it changes colors but keeps the same boring layout
Hiring a designer for a one-page site costs time and money you don't have for a quick project
after: 50 real design themes with distinct typography, color, and layout - not just color swaps
A browser-based lint pass catches common AI design patterns before you ship
One command to redesign or audit an existing page without starting over
uses_note: Hallmark is about 6 months old. Independent use reports are thin - most discussion is by developers comparing it to other design skills.

steps: Install the skill: run `npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g` in your terminal (needs Node 18+)

Open [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/) (or Cursor, Codex, or OpenCode) and type `/hallmark` followed by what you want to build - for example, `/hallmark a landing page for a weekend pottery workshop`
Review the result - the skill opens it in your browser and runs a lint pass. To redesign an existing page, try `/hallmark redesign index.html`

footprint.disk: The skill itself is a set of text files and about 755 reference photos. Total size is no data found.
footprint.memory: Runs inside your coding tool - no separate process. Browser checks need Chrome or Chromium installed.
footprint.runs_on: Any machine that runs Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, OpenCode, or GitHub Copilot. Needs Node 18+ for install. Browser lint checks need Chrome.

best_for: Anyone who uses AI to build web pages and wants them to look hand-designed
Non-designers who want real design themes, not just color changes
People who want to audit existing AI-built pages for generic patterns
skip_if: You already have a designer or a design system you follow
You don't build web pages with an AI coding tool
You need a full design tool, not a prompt skill - Hallmark guides the AI, it doesn't replace Figma

alternatives.name: Impeccable
alternatives.line: A broader design vocabulary with 24 commands (polish, bolder, critique, audit and more) from the creator of jQuery UI

alternatives.name: taste-skill
alternatives.line: A skill focused on giving your AI 'good taste' in design, with a different philosophy

alternatives.name: Impeccable
alternatives.line: A design vocabulary for your AI agent with polish, critique, and audit commands

watch: **Design is subjective.** The skill enforces its own design opinions - 50 themes and a lint pass for 'AI slop'. Your taste may differ, and the AI still makes the final choices.
**Browser checks need Chrome.** The lint pass opens your page in a real browser. Static checks work without it, but the full review needs Chrome or Chromium installed.
**No tagged releases.** Install is via npx from the main branch. The skill updates whenever the repo changes.
**The photos are openly licensed, but check the credits.** Hallmark includes about 755 photos from Wikimedia Commons, each credited on the generated page.
